📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Fatima Weiss. Trail crew lead. From Minneapolis, USA. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Lucky Coin, Dead Phone, Trail compass, Seed packet, Dispatcher's headset. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
A man, maybe 40s, with tattooed arms: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

You clutch your Lucky Coin, Dead Phone, Trail compass, Seed packet, Dispatcher's headset. You're still here.
